description:
FILED s483a (Opus, 2026-09-13) from the #1592 probes.  PRE-EXISTING on main
eabff00d (probed there; unchanged by #1592's fix).

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    my $cr = sub { 7 };
    my $v = eval { $cr->[0] };
    print defined $v ? "[$v]" : "undef", " err=[$@]\n";
    perl:  undef err=[Not an ARRAY reference at ...]
    PCL:   [CODE(0x1)] err=[]        <- the subscript hands back the code ref

CAUSE, LOCATED (not guessed): `p-aref-deref` has a deliberate arm

    ;; Function as single-element list: (sub{...})[0] = the sub itself
    ((functionp arr) (if (eql i 0) (make-p-box arr) *p-undef*))

because TWO different perl spellings lower to the SAME runtime entry: the
LIST SLICE `(sub { 7 })[0]` (perl: the code ref, a one-element list) and the
ARROW SUBSCRIPT `$cr->[0]` (perl: the fatal).  Verified by reading the
emission of both (`./pl2cl`): both produce `(p-aref-deref â¦)`.  So this is the
#1592 task's hypothesis (b) â "a non-deref spelling lowered into the same
runtime entry" â at a different site: it is REAL here, and it is NOT what
blocked the CODE referent rule at `${...}` (that was the check level; see
#1592's finding).

FIX SHAPE: the two spellings must stop sharing the entry â the list-slice
lowering should not emit `p-aref-deref` (or must mark itself), after which the
functionp arm becomes `(%p-not-a-ref "ARRAY")` and joins the referent-rule
family.  That is an EMITTER change (Pl/), so it carries corpus-diff +
emission-ab + a generation bump; it was out of #1592's scope (a `cl/`-only
runtime task) and is filed rather than bolted on.

SIBLINGS to check in the same session: `$cr->{k}` (perl: "Not a HASH
reference") and the write forms `$cr->[0] = 1` / `$cr->{k} = 1`.

=== DONE (s483b) ===
FIXED IN THE RUNTIME -- one line -- and THE TASK'S PREDICTED EMITTER CHANGE IS
NOT NEEDED.  That is the finding.

The task's cause is right about the shared entry and wrong about the
consequence: both spellings do call `p-aref-deref`, but with DIFFERENT
OPERANDS.  A list-slice operand is wrapped by the emitter in `(vector â¦)` and
normalised by %p-listslice-array, so `(sub{7})[0]` arrives as a one-element
VECTOR and takes the ordinary p-aref arm; only a `$coderef->[i]` / `${$cr}[i]`
/ `$$cr[i]` deref reaches the entry as a BARE FUNCTION.  The `functionp` arm
(added April 2026, 7818b23f, for the codegen of the day, which did hand the
slice over bare) has therefore served only the deref for a long time.

MEASURED before deciding: with the arm replaced by `(%p-not-a-ref "ARRAY")`,
all 24 shapes of scratch/s483b/probes/b1618.pl are identical to perl 5.40.3 --
the five deref spellings die, and the whole slice family ((sub{7})[0],
(sub{7},sub{8})[1], ($cr)[0], ($cr)[1] = undef, (mk())[1], mixed lists, an
array in slice position) is UNMOVED.  The siblings the task asked about were
already right: `$cr->{k}` and both write forms died before this change.

So: no Pl/ change, no generation bump, no corpus-diff/emission-ab legs (nothing
under Pl/ changed).  Guard Pl/t/ref-to-ref-01.t 36 -> 39 -- the five deref
spellings, the slice family asserted UNMOVED, and the ARRAY/HASH siblings --
inverse-verified on a `git archive e3767cff` extraction (row 37 fails there;
rows 38-39 are negatives and pass on both sides).

BARS (shared with #1619, same batch): gate 235/8081 xs-only; full sweep --jobs 4
GATE clean, TOTAL 18675 (+0), drops 5 = census; companion op/ref.t 202/40,
op/bless.t 111/6, op/array.t 171/24, op/anonsub.t 1/5 = snapshot, ROW DIFF 0 NEW
/ 0 FIXED / 0 LOST; ir-conform 321 pass / 0 fail / 24 known / 0 stale.

RESIDUE FILED: #1621 -- an ESCAPED `\$cr` in a double-quoted string counts as a
string USE for the raw-slot verdict, so a CODE ref is stringified into its own
slot and LOST.  Found because an extended probe file's EARLIER rows answered
wrongly on account of text further down; verified byte-identical on the base
tree, and PCL_NO_RAW_VERDICT=1 is the discriminator.
subject: `$coderef->[0]` returns the code ref where perl dies "Not an ARRAY reference" -- the list slice `(sub{..})[0]` and the arrow subscript share p-aref-deref's functionp arm
